html:
The Petun, or Tionontati, were an Iroquoian people of southern Ontario, living south of Georgian Bay on Lake Huron. The French called them the Tobacco People, from the tobacco they grew and traded. They were close kin and allies of the Huron, and spoke a similar language.

Like the Huron and the Neutral, they lived in palisaded villages of longhouses and grew maize, beans and squash. French Jesuits of the Society of Jesus set up missions among them in the 1630s and 1640s.

In 1649 and 1650 the Haudenosaunee destroyed the Huron and then the Petun in the Beaver Wars. The survivors fled west with Huron refugees, and together they became the Wyandot, who later lived in Ohio, Michigan, Kansas and Oklahoma.
